newsitem.title: NORWAY: BNbank says DnB bid is good.
newsitem.headline: BNbank says DnB bid is good.

text.p: Norwegian mortgage lender Bolig og Naeringsbanken (BNbank) on Friday said a new takeover bid by Den norske Bank (DnB) appeared to be good and said it was postponing possible merger talks with rival bidder Fokus Bank.
Separately, BNbank's biggest shareholder, financial institution Den Nordenfjelske Bykredittforening, announced it was accepting DnB's new bid, which was presented on Thursday.
It said in a statement it was prepared to sell its 10 percent stake in BNbank to DnB.
DnB, Norway's biggest bank, raised its bid by 12 crowns to 207 crowns per share, including a dividend of 10.50 crowns.
DnB also announced the group had increased its shareholding in BNbank to 27.34 percent of stock, including options amounting to 18.59 percent.
DnB spokesman Jarl Veggan said following the latest developments the bank scented victory in the battle over BNbank.
"Now that we control 37 percent of the shares we have great faith that this will work out," Veggan told Reuters.
Fokus Bank declined comment on BNbank's statement.
BNbank's board said it was postponing possible merger talks with Fokus until the deadline for DnB's bid expired and the outcome of its takeover attempt was known.
BNbank shareholders were given until the end of April to accept the bid.
"The board has studied DnB's cash offer and has reached the conclusion that the bid appears to be good, given the value of BNbank," the statement said.
"The board, on the basis of the information it has received, is of the view that the interests of the employees will be safeguarded," it said. "The board was unanimous in its decision."

DnB's offer valued BNbank at 1.92 billion crowns excluding dividend. Its bid is conditional on DnB acquiring more than 90 percent of BNbank, that regulatory authorities approve of the acquisition and that no significant changes occur in BNbank's financial position.
Fokus, Norway's fourth biggest bank and the first to bid for BNbank, last month raised its original share exchange offer to value BNbank at 2.06 billion crowns following DnB's initial cash bid.
